summary.headline: Axiscades Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 42% YoY to ₹346 crore, but reported PAT loss of ₹14.8 crore; normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter of the divestment-led transition: Engineering Services is shown as discontinued operations (₹163 crore revenue), leaving continuing operations at ₹183 crore, up 94% YoY. Reported EBITDA for the combined business was ₹27.9 crore, with one-offs of ₹13.1 crore (including ₹9.62 crore receivable provision on an aged defence transaction and ₹3.5 crore hedge provision) and ₹21.81 crore divestment transaction cost below EBITDA. Management says normalized EBITDA was ₹41 crore (11.8% margin) and normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore. Guidance was reaffirmed: FY27 continuing revenue of ₹1,377 crore, EBITDA of ₹270 crore and PAT of about 50% of that, with acquisitions and divestment proceeds central to delivery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 continuing operations revenue guidance reaffirmed at ₹1,377 crore on an annualized pro forma basis.
FY27 EBITDA target of ₹270 crore; PAT expected at roughly 50% of EBITDA (~₹135 crore), could be higher with lower interest after debt paydown.
Defence revenue expected to grow over 75% YoY in FY27 and over the following years; ESAI/XiDA expected to grow over 100% this year.
Aerospace manufacturing target: annualized run rate of ₹375 crore revenue and ₹84 crore EBITDA by Q4 FY27, with the platform aiming at ~₹1,000 crore by FY29.
Power 930 targets (FY30 PAT of ₹960 crore) stated as unchanged.
Deferred ~₹140-142 crore revenue: ~40% (over ₹60 crore) recovered in Q1; balance planned across Q2 and Q3.
capex_capacity: Akkodis divestment valued at US$237 million (~₹2,256 crore); Phase 1 targeted by Aug 31 with ~₹190 crore post-tax cash; Phase 2 by Nov 30 (management later said it is trying to pull it to about September) bringing ~₹525 crore cash.
Extraordinary gain of ~₹1,255 crore to be recognised on closing; ~₹200+ crore expected in Q2, the bulk in Q3 (or late Q2).
Aerospace services divestment expected to close in Q2 FY27; combined divestment proceeds ~₹920 crore cited.

Devanahalli AeroLand Complex (DAL) commissioned; Devanahalli Atmanirbhar Complex (DAC) construction ongoing on 20 acres; Missile Atmanirbhar Complex in Hyderabad groundbreaking early July, construction begun; Center for Advanced Manufacturing (240,000 sq ft, 20 acres) being planned.
PP&E rose ₹40 crore in one quarter for Power 930 ramp-up. CapEx to be matched to inflows, with a short-term bridge facility; actual drawdown not more than ₹100-150 crore.
demand_pricing: Defence assured forecast visibility rose to ₹4,557 crore after ~₹332 crore of new wins; management says it converts over ~3 years to FY30. Total pipeline cited at ~₹24,000 crore.

Wins include BrahMos and anti-tank missile onboard electronics (development-cum-production), helicopter ERP, Uttam radar antenna beam control, and a 30 kW laser directed energy weapon technology transfer.
LUH Maritime order visibility of ₹150-170 crore this year, stated as backed by confirmed orders.
MBDA test bench programme: about 5 test benches per year for 3 years; launcher maintenance expanding with a Rafale-linked order.
Aerospace: non-binding offer signed for an AS9100 precision manufacturer; FY27 revenue ~₹180 crore and EBITDA ~₹39 crore (22% margin) annualized, due diligence to complete in Q2.
BrahMos NG seeker: prototype in advanced stage; seeker business expected from next financial year (FY28).

qa_highlights.question: Why divest the profitable aerospace services business when the company wants to build aerospace manufacturing, and could both have been done together?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to shift from services to product and solutions, citing OEM consolidation in services and a sale price that let proceeds fund Power 930 without equity dilution. KP Mohanakrishnan conceded doing both together was hypothetically possible but said the strategy chose product-based growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the Rs 10 crore receivable provision, Rs 3.5 crore hedge provision and Rs 22 crore deal cost booked?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shashidhar SK said the ~Rs 21 crore transaction cost sits in discontinued operations as an exceptional item, visible in the notes. The hedge unwinding of Rs 3.5 crore sits in continuing other expenses. Provisions of about Rs 6.5 crore (Ministry of Defence order) and Rs 3.14 crore (a defence PSU) were also cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalized PAT outlook for FY27 on Rs 1,377 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukund Santhanam reiterated FY27 EBITDA of Rs 270 crore and PAT broadly around 50% of that, about Rs 135 crore, possibly higher as divestment proceeds pay down debt and cut interest. He confirmed the analyst's view that Q2-Q4 would ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Status and timing of acquisitions, and what happens in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Two acquisitions (aerospace AS9100 manufacturer, XiDA business transfer) are targeted to close this quarter, with a third aerospace deal targeted by Q4. Management said most acquisitions will be in place by FY27-end and later ones will be smaller in scale than this year's.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Rs 4,557 crore defence assured visibility take to execute, and what is the wider pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharadhi Babu said the visibility is to be covered before FY30, about 3 years, with possible spillover into a fourth year. The total pipeline is about Rs 24,000 crore across unmanned systems, missiles, radar and DEW. Management also reiterated 75%+ defence growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power 930 target (FY30 PAT Rs 960 crore) still intact, and is the acquisition-led plan at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukund Santhanam said the Power 930 targets remain firm, with FY30 PAT of Rs 960 crore. He acknowledged acquisitions are binary, saying aerospace and XiDA are at advanced stages while other deals are still at non-binding offer stage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the year-wise CapEx plans and how will they be funded before divestment proceeds arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give year-wise CapEx, saying spend will be timed to inflows (Q2 and Q3 FY27, then FY28 and FY29) and to partner readiness. A short-term bridge facility will fund the gap, with actual drawdown not more than Rs 100-150 crore. Shashidhar SK also said Rs 200+ crore of gain is expected in Q2 and the bulk in early Q3.

risks_watch: Closing timelines: Akkodis Phase 1 (~Rs 190 crore post-tax cash) targeted by Aug 31; Phase 2 (~Rs 525 crore) targeted by Nov 30, with management trying to pull it to about September. Slippage delays the Rs 1,255 crore extraordinary gain and debt paydown.

Acquisition execution: aerospace (AS9100 manufacturer, non-binding offer, due diligence in Q2), XiDA business transfer and a third aerospace deal by Q4 are needed to rebuild EBITDA to Rs 270 crore. Several other deals are still non-binding.
Recovery of the Rs 9.62 crore receivable provision on an aged defence transaction, which is being pursued with the Ministry of Defence.
Deferred revenue of about Rs 140-142 crore: over Rs 60 crore recovered in Q1, with the balance planned across Q2 and Q3.
Continuing business still does not cover finance cost (Rs 8.9 crore) and depreciation (Rs 8.8 crore); ADD Solutions loss (EBITDA -Rs 4.8 crore) to be exited by Q4 FY27 via a sale process.
Aerospace manufacturing: Rs 6.1 crore Q1 revenue with negative EBITDA and a 30-member team ahead of revenue. Run rate target of Rs 375 crore revenue and Rs 84 crore EBITDA by Q4 FY27 is a steep ramp.
Capacity build and bridge borrowing: CapEx is not guided year-wise, and a short-term bridge facility is planned. Monitor PP&E growth and debt levels against the no-material-long-term-debt commitment.

Defence concentration: defence is over two-thirds of continuing revenue; LUH Maritime Rs 150-170 crore visibility is said to be backed by confirmed orders. Q1 defence reported EBITDA was Rs 2.6 crore after about Rs 9.6 crore one-time costs.
key_quotes: The divestment of the non-core and services business is largely complete, only ADD solutions remain and its exit is under way.
This quarter, uh, we have delivered the highest revenue in the company's history, and we also reported a net loss.

We expect PAT to be broadly around about 50% of that number. It could be higher because we'll actually have a lesser we'll have proceeds from the divestment that would be available to us that will help us pay down some of our debt and reduce our interest costs.
Our Power 930 targets remain still, still absolutely, uh, firm.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on strategy, growth and the divestment path, but defensive and evasive on specifics. Management gave no year-wise CapEx or acquisition-by-acquisition financials, deferred some questions, and relied on a technical outage and 'to be announced' answers to avoid detail.
